html:
The brown tree snake reached Guam by accident, probably in military cargo after the Second World War. With no predators, it spread across the island and wiped out most of Guam's native forest birds.

By the 1980s the forests had fallen almost silent. Several bird species vanished from the wild, and the Guam rail survived only through breeding in captivity. The snake also causes frequent power cuts by climbing lines.

Without birds to spread seeds, the forests themselves began to change. The US has tried traps, dogs and even dropping poisoned mice from helicopters. It is one of the best-known cases of an invasive species, like cane toads and rabbits in Australia. See also Battle of Guam.
